https://www.barrons.com/articles/at-t-shares-look-ripe-for-buying-1537552511 AT&T Shares Look Ripe for Buying By Sept. 21, 2018 1:55 p.m. ET Text Size Sept. 21, 2018 1:55 p.m. ET
AT&T is rising on Friday, helped by an upgrade from UBS .
Where we were : AT&T has lagged this year, like other telecom stocks, although company-specific worries also weighed on the shares.
Where we’re headed : UBS argues that attractive valuation and improving wireless trends will boost the shares.
Shares of AT&T (T) have fallen more than 12% this year, but the worst looks like it’s past, argues UBS’s John Hodulik : He upgraded the shares to Buy from Neutral and raised his price target by $5, to $38.
Telecom—the sector soon to be replaced by communication services—hasn’t had a great year, and AT&T specifically has been hurt by worries about the integration of Time Warner and its debt, along with necessary network investments. However, Hodulik sees much of these pressures already priced into the beleaguered shares, given that they’re trading not far off all-time valuation lows (with the widest gap between AT&T and Verizon Communications ’ (VZ) multiple in years).
Moreover, wireless, accounting for half of AT&T’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, is still crucial, and on that front he points to improving average revenue per user (APRU) across the industry, with fewer promotions around Apple ’s (AAPL) iPhone, highlighting a less cutthroat competitive environment. If the Sprint (S)/ T-Mobile US (TMUS) deal goes through, that should “solidify” this benign competitive situation, but even if it doesn’t, other carriers’ inability to invest in 5G means that AT&T and Verizon should still reap outsized benefits.
On the Time Warner side, he notes that WarnerMedia faces easier comparables in the second half of the year, although higher costs and ratings declines do “temper” his expectations.
AT&T is up 1.7% to $34 this afternoon.
